title.official: The Guiding Manual on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Use in Member States of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)
title.english: The Guiding Manual on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Use in Member States of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)

dates.notes: The cover is dated "Version 1.0 | November 2023". No exact adoption day or formal adoption instrument is printed. A GCC Secretariat news item of 7 October 2025 lists the manual among the Council's achievements, and Bahrain's Information & eGovernment Authority states that the manual was issued by the Ministerial Committee for eGovernment.

status_note: Non-binding guidance approved for use by GCC member states; it is not a treaty and creates no signature, ratification or depositary regime. The acquired official English text is version 1.0 dated November 2023.

legal_nature.rationale: The text is a guiding manual addressed to GCC member states and relevant entities. It contains no treaty, signature, ratification, depositary, entry-into-force or enforcement clause; it expressly states that it does not replace or override the duties or rights of states.

relevance.reason: The first GCC-wide AI ethics instrument located in official sources. It records a 2023 subregional consensus framework that sits between the 2025 Arab Charter and national AI policies, and it is directly relevant to the project's coverage of regional AI governance in the Middle East.
ai_provisions: respect for Islamic Sharia, national constitutions and Gulf unity
peaceful use of AI for the well-being of GCC citizens
protection of vulnerable groups and accessibility
national implementation through policies, legislation and ethics committees
relevance.excluded_scope: The manual is non-binding guidance. It does not create directly enforceable rights or obligations, and it does not prescribe a regional enforcement, supervision or dispute-settlement mechanism.

languages.note: Arabic is the original language of the GCC manual. The acquired 14-page English version 1.0 (November 2023) is an official GCC/Bahrain publication and is the version read for this record; the Arabic original was not acquired. No language-authenticity clause was located.

sources.publisher: Gulf Cooperation Council / Kingdom of Bahrain
sources.note: "The Guiding Manual on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Use in Member States of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), Version 1.0" - official 14-page English PDF dated November 2023, hosted on Bahrain's national portal. It was read end-to-end and segmented into 14 page units.

Official GCC Secretariat news item dated 7 October 2025. It lists "the guiding manual on the ethics of artificial intelligence use" among the achievements reported to the Supreme Council and attributes it to the Ministerial Committee for Digital Government.

sources.publisher: Information & eGovernment Authority, Kingdom of Bahrain
sources.note: Official Bahraini page dated 27 July 2025. It states that the GCC AI Ethics Manual was issued by the Ministerial Committee for eGovernment and adopted alongside Bahrain's National AI Policy.

rights.note: Official government publication reproduced for research. The PDF is stored unaltered; no relicense is asserted.

The committee's English name varies between the 2023 PDF, the 2025 GCC Secretariat account and Bahrain's 2025 page; the record preserves the variation rather than choosing one.

text.extraction_note: Extracted from the official 14-page English PDF with pypdf. The text is clean; page 1 contains the title and version line, and pages 2-14 contain the contents, values, principles and final provisions.

gaps: The manual is non-binding guidance; no enforceable obligations or review mechanism are created.
No exact adoption day, formal decision number or complete list of approving states is printed in the acquired text.
The Arabic original was not acquired; this record relies on the official English version.
National implementation, designated ethics committees and practical use of the manual are not assessed.

The issuing committee appears as the Ministerial Committee for eGovernment in the 2023 PDF and Bahrain's 2025 page, and as the Ministerial Committee for Digital Government in the GCC Secretariat's 2025 account.

assertions.note: The official PDF is a non-binding GCC manual, version 1.0 dated November 2023; no exact adoption day is printed.
The manual contains four values and seven ethical principles with implementation recommendations.

provenance.notes: Bahrain attributes the manual to the Ministerial Committee for eGovernment; the GCC Secretariat calls that committee the Ministerial Committee for Digital Government. The record preserves both official formulations.
